title: Annual North Korean Defector Arrivals in South Korea
publisher: Ministry of Unification (대한민국 통일부)
latest_value: 2025: 223 persons; 2026-H1: 63 persons (cumulative: 34,575)
compare: China border arrests, internal refugee estimates, separated families
presentation: Published in scattered tables on unikorea.go.kr and annual Ministry PDFs, frequently locked behind domestic IP filters; difficult for non-Korean researchers to track historically.
chart_idea: Line chart showing the rise from Arduous March (1998: 71), peak under Kim Jong Il (2009: 2,914), collapse under COVID border closure (2021: 63, 2022: 67), and modest rebound (2024: 236, 2025: 223).
notes: Verified via data.go.kr dataset 15106185 (modified 2026-09-30) and MOU July 2026 briefing. Complete annual dataset compiled in samples/rights/mou_defector_arrivals_annual.csv.

title: North Korean Defector Arrivals in South Korea by Gender
publisher: Ministry of Unification (대한민국 통일부)
latest_value: 2025: 25 male / 198 female (88.8% female); 2026-H1: 4 male / 59 female (93.7% female)
compare: Global UNHCR refugee gender distributions, economic labor migration flows
presentation: Separated into annual summary PDF columns without interactive multi-line or stacked percentage visualization.
chart_idea: Stacked 100% area chart showing gender reversal: pre-2002 was majority male (1998: 77% male), but post-2002 shifted dramatically to over 70-85% female as women gained mobility through informal jangmadang trading.
notes: Women make up over 72% of cumulative defectors (24,800+ women out of 34,500+). In 2026 H1, 59 of 63 arrivals were female (93.7%).

title: Cumulative North Korean Defector Population in South Korea
publisher: Ministry of Unification (대한민국 통일부)
latest_value: 2026-H1: 34,575 cumulative escapees
compare: South Korea municipal population benchmarks, overseas diaspora populations
presentation: Published as a single static metric on Ministry splash pages; historical cumulative trajectory is not plotted.
chart_idea: Cumulative sigmoid growth curve demonstrating rapid linear growth between 2002 and 2011 (passing 10,000 in 2007, 20,000 in 2010, 30,000 in 2016), plateauing sharply post-2020.
notes: Verified from KOSIS table DT_1ZGAA42 and Ministry of Unification official statistical briefings.

title: North Korean Defectors by DPRK Origin Province
publisher: Ministry of Unification & Korea Hana Foundation (남북하나재단)
latest_value: 2025: North Hamgyong 58.2%, Ryanggang 16.4%, South Hamgyong 9.1%, Pyongyang 3.5%, Jagang 1.1%, other 11.7%
compare: DPRK official population distribution by province, Chinese mobile phone coverage reach
presentation: Published in Hana Foundation Settlement Survey tables in Korean; English readers rarely see that ~75% of all defectors come from just two northern border provinces.
chart_idea: Choropleth map of North Korea shaded by defector origin density alongside a bar chart contrasting province population share vs defector share (highlighting the massive overrepresentation of Hamgyong and Ryanggang).
notes: Essential epistemological context for all defector testimony: our intelligence window into everyday DPRK life is heavily concentrated along the Tumen and Yalu river border zones.

title: Pre-Escape Occupation Profile of North Korean Defectors
publisher: Ministry of Unification & Korea Hana Foundation
latest_value: 2025: Unemployed/Housewives 48.6%, Manual Workers 36.1%, Service/Merchants 7.8%, Officials/Intelligentsia 2.5%, Military 1.8%
compare: DPRK official labor force distribution, South Korea employment sectors
presentation: Buried in annual settlement surveys with changing classification categories.
chart_idea: Categorical stacked bar chart showing how housewives and informal market workers dominate defection flows, while state officials and military personnel represent small but strategically significant fractions.
notes: The high percentage of 'unemployed' corresponds to married women excluded from official state workplace rosters who operate in informal jangmadang markets.

title: Documented Forced Repatriations from China to North Korea
publisher: Database Center for North Korean Human Rights (NKDB / 북한인권정보센터)
latest_value: 2026: 8,245 cumulative documented refoulement cases across 11 border detention points
compare: MOU arrival counts (the inverse filter: arrivals vs refoulements), UNHCR global refoulement tracking
presentation: Serialized inside SvelteKit devalue arrays on visualatlas.org and in NKDB research monographs; never presented as a clean public time series.
chart_idea: Dual-axis time series comparing annual defector arrivals in South Korea against documented repatriations from China, demonstrating how border tightening simultaneously drove down arrivals and surged refoulement risk.
notes: NKDB March 2026 report 'The Machinery Behind the Forced Repatriation of North Koreans in China' catalogues 8,245 cases across 20+ years, detailing processing at Tumen, Hunchun, Longjing, and Dandong.

title: Post-COVID Forced Returns of North Koreans from China
publisher: Human Rights Watch (HRW)
latest_value: 2024-2025: 406 documented returns; total post-2020: 1,076+ returns (including Oct 2023 mass expulsion of 500-600)
compare: Border security fencing expansion, China border security arrests
presentation: Scattered press releases and advocacy letters to UN bodies.
chart_idea: Timeline bar chart highlighting specific documented mass refoulement operations (e.g. October 2023: 500-600 people through 5 border crossings, April 2024: 60 people, late 2025: 120 people).
notes: Verified from HRW reports citing Chinese detention centers in Jilin and Liaoning provinces and firsthand defector network communications.

title: Transnational Repatriation and Secret Detention Network
publisher: Transitional Justice Working Group (TJWG)
latest_value: 2026: Documented embassy holding cells in Beijing and 4 primary crossing gates (Tumen, Dandong, Hunchun, Nanping)
compare: NKPD border detention facilities, Visual Atlas China detention hubs
presentation: Geographic findings published in PDF reports without machine-readable coordinates or time series.
chart_idea: Sankey flow diagram illustrating the repatriation pipeline: Escape into Northeast China -> Detention in Chinese Border PSB Detention Centers -> Transfer to DPRK Border City MSS/MPS Holding Centers (Jipkyolso) -> Forced Labor sentencing in Kyo-hwa-so or Kwanliso.
notes: Corroborates NKPD and Visual Atlas findings on North Hamgyong Provincial MPS Holding Center as the primary intake node for repatriated escapees.

title: NKPD Documented Right to Life Violations (Executions and Lethal Abuse)
publisher: Korea Future (North Korean Prison Database)
latest_value: 2018: 1 case; peak 2005: 32 cases; total: 210 verified Right to Life violations
compare: Amnesty International global death penalty statistics, TJWG public execution sites
presentation: Buried in the Uwazi backend API without public time-series charts on nkpd.io.
chart_idea: Time series bar chart showing annual documented Right to Life violations across 30 years (peak during 2002–2006 anti-market and border crossing crackdowns).

title: TJWG Documented Public Execution Locations and Decadal Frequency
publisher: Transitional Justice Working Group (TJWG)
latest_value: 2019 report: 323 public execution sites and 25 body disposal sites identified from 610 testimonies
compare: NKPD penal facilities, satellite-observed airfield/riverbed execution grounds
presentation: Published in GIS spatial reports with blurred coordinates to protect ground witnesses and sites.
chart_idea: Histogram of documented public executions by decade (1960s through 2010s) showing the surge during the 1990s famine and 2000s market crackdowns.
notes: Covers executions for economic 'crimes' (theft of state property/machinery/copper, livestock slaughter) and ideological infractions (watching South Korean DVDs).

title: Statutory Capital Crimes in North Korea's Penal Framework
publisher: Korea Institute for National Unification (통일연구원 KINU)
latest_value: 2026 White Paper: 11 capital offenses in Criminal Code + mandatory capital penalties in 4 special statutes
compare: China Criminal Law death penalty articles, South Korea abolished-in-practice status
presentation: Documented in academic Korean PDF white papers; legal evolution is not tracked visually.
chart_idea: Timeline chart tracking the legislative expansion of capital crimes under Kim Jong Un: 2015 Criminal Code (8 offenses) -> Revision (11 offenses) -> Anti-Reactionary Culture Act (2020) -> Youth Education Guarantee Act (2021) -> Pyongyang Cultural Language Protection Act (2023) -> Emergency Quarantine Law.
notes: Crucial legal indicator: despite claims of judicial modernization, DPRK has continually widened capital punishment to suppress foreign media, language influence, and epidemic infractions.

title: NKDB Integrated North Korean Human Rights Violation Archives
publisher: Database Center for North Korean Human Rights (NKDB)
latest_value: 2025: 146,136 total records (87,317 incidents and 56,452 persons in 2024 edition)
compare: South Korea Truth and Reconciliation Commission archives, German Stasi records archive
presentation: Presented as headline counts at annual press conferences and in physical white papers.
chart_idea: Multi-category area chart showing the growth of NKDB's documented incidents over the past 20 years broken down by right violated (Life, Liberty, Fair Trial, Movement).
notes: Verified from 2024 and 2025 NKDB White Paper releases. Represents the world's largest independent database of verified North Korean human rights abuses.

title: NKPD Documented Violations by Human Right Category
publisher: Korea Future (North Korean Prison Database)
latest_value: Total 9,149 violations: Health 1,995; Torture 1,622; Expression 1,576; Conscience/Religion 1,091; Liberty 901; Forced Labour 680
compare: Universal Declaration of Human Rights articles, ICCPR reporting benchmarks

chart_idea: Horizontal bar chart of rights violations showing that bodily survival rights (Right to Health: 1,995; Torture: 1,622) and speech/belief rights (Expression: 1,576; Conscience: 1,091) constitute over 70% of documented abuses.
notes: Verified live from NKPD API. Category counts: Health: 1,995; Torture: 1,622; Expression: 1,576; Conscience: 1,091; Liberty: 901; Forced Labour: 680; SGBV: 469; Fair Trial: 348; Life: 210; Children: 204; Disability: 53. Total: 9,149.

title: NKPD Documented Violations Time Series by Incident Year

title: NKPD Geocoded Penal Facilities by Administrative Category
publisher: Korea Future (North Korean Prison Database)

presentation: Map exists on nkpd.io, but summary statistics by category and agency are not easily exportable.
chart_idea: Donut chart of facility types coupled with an organizational breakdown (Ministry of Social Security vs Ministry of State Security vs Local People's Committees).
notes: Verified live from NKPD database. 103 of 245 facilities have precise GPS coordinates, administrative province, and managing body.

title: Kwanliso (Political Prison Camp) Total Inmate Population Estimates
publisher: UN COI, HRNK, US State Dept, Amnesty International, KINU
latest_value: 2026 consensus estimate: 80,000–120,000 prisoners across Camps 14, 16, 18, 25 (down from ~200,000 in 1990s/2000s)
compare: Soviet Gulag peak populations, Xinjiang internment estimates, world incarceration rates per capita
presentation: Published as narrative estimates scattered across dozens of individual human rights reports with no centralized historical comparison table.
chart_idea: Range chart (shaded confidence band between lower and upper estimates) with annotated dots for landmark publications: 1990 State Dept (150k-200k), 2002 Hidden Gulag 1st Ed (150k-200k), 2011 Amnesty (200k), 2014 UN COI (80k-120k), 2025 KINU (80k-120k).
notes: Compiled and verified in samples/rights/kwanliso_population_estimates.csv. Documents the downward revision driven by the closure of Camp 22 (2012) and Camp 15 (2020), balanced by extreme mortality rates.

title: Operational Status and Camp Count of Political Prison Camps
publisher: HRNK / David Hawk / Bermudez / KINU
latest_value: 2026: 4 active camps (Camp 14 Kaechon, 16 Hwasong, 18 Bukchang, 25 Chongjin); Camp 15 dismantled ~2020; Camp 22 closed 2012
compare: Total land area reserved for camps (~1,500 sq km, roughly the size of Greater London)
presentation: Detailed satellite imagery analyses exist, but camp status transitions are rarely displayed on a unified timeline.
chart_idea: Step line chart showing the consolidation of Kwanliso facilities from ~14 camps in the 1980s down to 10 in the 1990s, 6 in the 2000s, 5 in 2012, and 4 today.
notes: Operational status ground-truthed against HRNK satellite imagery reports and KINU White Papers. Polygons mapped in free-north-korea camps.geojson.

title: UN General Assembly DPRK Human Rights Resolution Voting History
publisher: United Nations Dag Hammarskjöld Library / General Assembly Plenary
latest_value: 2025 (A/RES/80/220): Adopted without a vote (Consensus); recorded votes held 2005–2011, 2013–2015
compare: UNGA votes on Myanmar, Syria, Crimea, Iran human rights resolutions
presentation: UN Digital Library is locked behind AWS WAF challenge; Harvard Dataverse provides the clean roll-call dataset.
chart_idea: Stacked bar chart of annual voting tallies (Yes, No, Abstain, Consensus indicator) alongside a world choropleth map showing diplomatic alignment on DPRK human rights (Western democracies + allies vs DPRK/China/Russia bloc vs Non-Aligned abstainers).
notes: Full voting tallies verified and saved in samples/rights/unga_dprk_resolutions_voting.csv. Shows increasing diplomatic isolation of DPRK culminating in routine consensus adoption.

title: UN Human Rights Council DPRK Resolution Adoption Timeline
publisher: Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR)
latest_value: 2026: Adopted by consensus; 2014 resolution (HRC 25/25) adopted 30 Yes, 6 No, 11 Abstain following Kirby COI report
compare: Universal Periodic Review (UPR) third and fourth cycle recommendations accepted vs rejected by DPRK
presentation: Reports published as formal UN meeting documents in PDF format; roll-call votes are recorded in session reports.
chart_idea: Milestone timeline chart showing key structural actions created by HRC resolutions: Special Rapporteur mandate (2004) -> Commission of Inquiry creation (2013) -> OHCHR Seoul field office establishment (2015) -> Accountability mechanism reinforcement (2024-2026).
notes: Verified from OHCHR session records. The 47-member council adopted DPRK resolutions by recorded vote in 2008-2011 and 2014-2015, and by consensus in 2012-2013 and 2016-2026.

title: Inter-Korean Separated Families: Living Survivors vs Deceased Applicants

publisher: Ministry of Unification

publisher: Ministry of Unification & Korean Red Cross (대한적십자사)

notes: Verified from Ministry of Unification Inter-Korean Exchange and Cooperation Portal.

title: DPRK Ballistic Missile Launches and Flight Tests by Year
publisher: CNS / NTI / nagix / free-north-korea
latest_value: 2025: 11 tests in baseline; 2026: 43 tests in baseline through 2026-09-20; 357 total tests 1984–2026
compare: Worldwide ballistic missile tests, Iranian missile tests, UNSC resolution adoptions

chart_idea: Stacked bar chart of launches by year broken down by missile class (SRBM, MRBM, IRBM, ICBM, SLBM) and test outcome (Success, Failure, Unknown).
notes: Verified from public/data/test.en.json. Shows dramatic escalation under Kim Jong Un (over 90% of all launches in DPRK history occurred since 2012).

title: North Korean Underground Nuclear Tests Chronology and Seismic Yield
publisher: USGS, CTBTO, NORSAR, South Korea KMA (기상청)
latest_value: Test 6 (2017-09-03): mb 6.3, estimated yield 100–250 kt (thermonuclear weapon); zero tests 2018–2026
compare: Hiroshima yield (15 kt), global nuclear tests since 1998, Indian/Pakistani 1998 nuclear tests
presentation: Seismic magnitudes published immediately by USGS/CTBTO; yields estimated by research institutes.
chart_idea: Exponential bubble chart showing the explosive yield progression across the six tests at Punggye-ri: 2006 (0.7-2 kt) -> 2009 (2-4 kt) -> 2013 (6-9 kt) -> 2016-Jan (7-10 kt) -> 2016-Sep (10-20 kt) -> 2017-Sep (100-250 kt, over 10x Hiroshima).
notes: All 6 tests conducted at Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Facility, Kilju County, North Hamgyong Province. Tunnel collapses documented by seismic and satellite analysis.

title: Missile Dataset Freshness Audit: 2025–2026 Discrepancies vs Japan MOD and ROK JCS

compare: Japan EEZ impact reports, ROK radar track logs

notes: Documented in docs/research/missile_gaps.md and json. Public/data/test.en.json baseline ends on 2026-09-20, missing October 3, 2026 SRBM launch.

title: DPRK Official State Budget Share Allocated to National Defense
publisher: Supreme People's Assembly (SPA / 최고인민회의) / KCNA
compare: ROK defense budget share (~12.5% of national expenditure), US federal defense share (~13%)

notes: Official figures cover only operational line items; weapons development and nuclear/missile R&D are concealed under the Second Economic Committee and separate party funds.

publisher: US Department of State (WMEAT), Bank of Korea, KIDA, IISS
latest_value: WMEAT / KIDA estimate: 23%–26% of GDP (~$3.6B–$4.5B USD); world's highest defense burden

title: North Korean Penal Facilities Chronology by Era Established
